blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The International Date Line roughly follows the 180° meridian in the Pacific Ocean.
Crossing the line towards the west adds one calendar day.
Crossing the line towards the east subtracts one calendar day.
The line intentionally deviates from a straight path to keep unified dates across countries and island nations.
Frequently tested rule: Crossing West = Add 1 day; Crossing East = Subtract 1 day.
The IDL is located in the Pacific Ocean (180° longitude), not the Atlantic or Prime Meridian (0°).
Remember that the IDL is not a straight line because it zigzags/deviates to avoid splitting countries and islands.
